what: Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base full-weight trial on H100:2 (FSDP2, shared prefix, balanced micro-batches), experiments/sft-resume-e2e-08b.json on evals/v7/decision-v7, save_every_steps 50, Modal timeout 480 s with 2 retries (sft-resume-e2e-killed) against the same trial with timeout 3000 s (sft-resume-e2e-whole)
container_log: the container stdout of both trials (modal app logs kev-sft-infra-2, interleaved as streamed; the whole trial counts 0-1150, the killed one restarts at its resume points): commit lines from modal_app.commit_resume_points, the retries' 'continuing' lines and the saves. The killed trial committed point 300 before attempt 1 was killed at step ~320 and point 1050 before attempt 2 was killed at ~1080; a point that completed while a commit ran is committed with the next.
reading: Each attempt continued from the last committed point (300, then 1050) at the saved data position, and the 10-step loss windows logged again after a resume match the first time to the third decimal. The final weights differ from the uninterrupted run's, as two uninterrupted segments already do from step 10 (3.360 vs 3.366): these CUDA kernels are not bit-deterministic. Bit-identical continuation is proven on CPU (tests/test_unit.py::test_resume_is_bit_identical, 1 and 2 ranks).
